threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the Tube app for delays on weekends. In Hackney, it's all about the bus or just walking over to the next pub.
Caught the 59 last night; a guy put his feet up on the seat and started arguing with a seagull outside the window. Classic Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street musician playing a saxophone in front of a kebab shop, while locals argued over football, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that serves beer from a vending machine alongside karaoke in an abandoned factory. It's a vibe!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they instinctively know which Muni bus skips Civic Center during a dog-on-the-tracks delay—everyone else is still trying to figure out a Plan B.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where a guy was performing magic tricks for a crowd of commuters. Only in SF do you get a street show to pass the time.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists miss that the best vermut in Gràcia isn’t at fancy bars but at the corner shop where locals gather for a quick chat and a canya.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they keep looking up at the buildings, trying to figure out which one's modernista and which is just regular old.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the buses run on time and that people actually see the awful state of the roads. Welcome to reality!
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week and saw a guy trying to serenade a pigeon. The bird was having none of it, just pecked at the crumbs.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy juggling flaming torches at the U-Bahnhof in the middle of a Tuesday rush hour, I realized this place has a different rhythm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a 24-hour Turkish bakery with steaming simit on Sundays, where the smell alone pulls you in like a warm hug.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they don’t flinch at the sound of BART brakes screeching outside their window at 2 AM.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: The other day, I watched a bus stop mid-route because a lady was feeding the pigeons right on the tracks. Only in the TL, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the tiny artsy bars where locals gather, hidden in plain sight.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their hesitant order at cafes, still fumbling with the difference between 'café con leche' and 'latte'.
